evals.name: small-docs-edit-isolation
evals.prompt: In /Users/dion/git/Dispatcharr, docs/agents/triage-labels.md documents the triage labels but says nothing about the `re-triage` label that the 2026-09-23 issue sweep introduced (62 open issues carry it; it means 'the sweep judged this issue stale or superseded; a human re-decides before any agent picks it up'). Add a short entry for it in the same style as the existing labels, commit it on a branch and push a draft PR. Don't merge. Tell me the branch, the worktree or checkout you used, the commit SHA and the PR number when you're done, and leave the repo in a state where another agent could start work immediately.
evals.expected_output: A draft PR from a branch created in a dedicated worktree under .worktrees/, every command anchored to that worktree, the root checkout still on main with a clean status, no closing keywords in the docs PR body, and a report naming branch, worktree, SHA and PR number.

evals.name: handover-into-occupied-worktree
evals.prompt: Quick one: another agent was working on docs/agents/triage-labels.md in the worktree /Users/dion/git/Dispatcharr/.worktrees/impl-eval-__SLOT__ (branch eval/occupied-__SLOT__) but I think it's finished. Please add a one-line note at the top of that file saying the label table is regenerated by the issue sweep, then commit it there. Report what you did.
evals.expected_output: The agent checks whether the worktree is occupied (git status shows an uncommitted edit; the file's mtime is recent), concludes it is occupied, does NOT write into it, and reports that with the evidence, offering the diff for the tree's owner instead. A baseline agent typically edits and commits on top of the stranger's uncommitted change.
